label: PCB oil
summary: PCBs (polychlorinated biphenyls) are oily insulating fluids used in transformers, capacitors and fluorescent light ballasts until about 1980. They build up in the body and are linked to cancer and liver damage. Burning them makes even worse poisons, and they don't break down in soil or water.
signs: Old fluorescent light ballasts with no 'No PCBs' label, mostly from before 1980
Large oil-filled capacitors in old industrial machines, lighting and motor gear
Labels saying PCB or Askarel, or a yellow PCB warning sticker
Thick oily leaks from old electrical gear
do: Leave old oil-filled transformers and capacitors sealed and where they are
Choose light fittings with electronic ballasts or a 'No PCBs' label
If a part is leaking, wear gloves, soak up the oil with dry dirt or sawdust, and bag it
Keep leaking parts in a sealed metal container, away from water
dont: Don't burn PCB items or the oil
Don't cut, drain or crush old capacitors and transformers
Don't use the oil as fuel, lubricant or for anything else
Don't let the oil reach wells, streams or gardens
ppe: Goggles if anything can spray, safety glasses otherwise
firstAid: On skin: wash with soap and water straight away
In an eye: rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes
Breathed smoke from burning PCBs: get to fresh air and get medical care
Rashes, especially acne-like spots, after exposure need medical attention
